facts.text: Founded in 1915 as a neighborhood team, the Staten Island Stapletons joined the NFL from 1929 to 1932.
Jack Shapiro, the team’s blocking back, was the shortest player in NFL history, weighing just 119–126 pounds and standing barely over five feet tall.
In 1928 the Stapes posted a 10–1–1 record, the best season in their history, yet they never achieved a winning season in the NFL.
The neighborhood’s Tappen Park gives Stapleton a town‑square feel and hosts a mix of American diners, a gastropub, and Sri Lankan, Mexican, and Italian eateries.
Stapleton sits only a mile from the Staten Island Ferry and is just around the corner from the Stapleton train station, making it a quick hop to Manhattan.
The site of the farm where Cornelius Vanderbilt grew up now houses the Paramount Theater building on Bay Street, a landmark that closed in the early 1980s.
